component.name: Switch Frame Tap
component.summary: Watch and record your Switch, streamed over USB or the network

description.p: The PC viewer for Switch Frame Tap: watch, play and record the game running on your Nintendo Switch, streamed with sound over a USB-C cable or the network at the game's own resolution and 60 fps.

It needs a Switch running Atmosphère with the Switch Frame Tap sysmodule installed. The viewer decodes on the GPU (VAAPI or NVDEC), records MP4 and takes native-resolution screenshots, with optional FSR 1 and NIS upscaling.
USB needs the udev rule from the project page installed once on the host.

screenshot.caption: A Switch game streamed to a PC over USB

ul.li: SwitchU support: with SwitchU as the HOME menu, its menu streams from boot and HOME and back work while streaming.
Final Fantasy XII in handheld streams full size, and games that draw in X8R8G8B8 get the right colours.
Play the Switch from the viewer with a controller, the keyboard or the mouse (off by default), with a Controller menu for remapping.
The buttons over the picture fade out after 3 s without mouse movement; Alt-drag, Ctrl-wheel and Ctrl-click move and zoom the picture in fullscreen.
Faster streams in heavy scenes, and fixes for red pictures, stutters and missing sound in some games.
One file per recording is a setting now, off by default: recordings start a new file when the picture size changes and are never scaled.
No empty 0-second file when the picture size changes right as a recording starts.

description.p: Viewer unchanged; the Switch side lets homebrew from forwarders run in docked mode.

ul.li: Recordings stay one file: while the viewer records, the Switch keeps the picture at the size the recording started at.
Over USB the viewer repeats a request the Switch was not listening for yet.
A pin button keeps the window on top of others.
Over the network the viewer reconnects by itself after the Switch restarts or changes network, and waits calmly when another viewer already has the Switch.
Network viewers say why there is no picture, as USB viewers already did.
Games with dynamic resolution or a zoom in the middle of the picture (Super Mario Galaxy, Kingdom Hearts) are cropped and scaled by the viewer, sharper than on the console.
More games stream right: Super Mario 3D All-Stars, Sunshine, Doom 3 and Duke Nukem 3D; homebrew games stream their picture and sound.
The picture no longer goes black in a large window with sdl2-compat.
No latency spike every 3 seconds: the console writes nothing to its SD card while it streams.
The Album and System Settings stream again on firmware 23; the viewer says when the keyboard pauses the stream.
Native Wayland on KDE Plasma, and switch-frame-tap-viewer --check prints the session, drivers, udev rule, USB devices and network.
Stream the Switch's HOME menu and its overlays (volume bar, quick settings, power menu, Tesla/Ultrahand) - opt-in on the console.
Network streams show a picture right away when the viewer joins mid-game.
The viewer explains USB-C to USB-C cable trouble, and draws in software when no GPU driver works.
Fixed streaming stopping until a reboot after closing some homebrew apps.
Fullscreen on a screen that is not 16:9 now suggests a 16:9 mode.
Fixed black screen after launching many apps in a row.
Fixed boot crash on consoles with several sysmodules.
Super Mario Odyssey and similar games fill the stream in handheld instead of sitting in the top-left corner.
Uses much less system memory.
GPU decoding is on by default on Windows (D3D11VA) and Linux.
Smoother over Wi-Fi: the network stream sends a keyframe only every 4 s.
